HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Low worm's-eye two-shot from the grit at knee height in the palace yard of Sabi, late afternoon. Teenage Gyebek in dusty undyed white, locked chest to chest in a ssireum satba grip with a taller clan boy who leans over him and strains, face hidden by his own shoulder. Gyebek's jaw is set, eyes calm and level, heels sliding back a finger's width in the sand, sand spraying off his heel. The chalked square line cuts the foreground as the one device. Behind, out of focus, the stone hall steps crowded with silk-robed elders and young princes in bokeh. Low sun from the west rakes across both straining backs, long shadows across the grit, warm gold catching the sweat on Gyebek's neck. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = gyebek. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. GYEBEK — Now: Boyhood (ch_gyebek_boy): a thin nameless river boy of about thirteen, barefoot, in a plain undyed WHITE hemp shirt and trousers with a rope belt; short-to-medium loose black hair, no topknot, no cap, no headband, no scarf, no armor; flat, watchful, unblinking eyes. Colour #d9b13a. PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
